**Continuous 2.32.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.32.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.32.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.32.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.32.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.32.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.32.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.32.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.32.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.32.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.32.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.32.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.30.0

This release closes a security hole and makes it harder to lose work. `@url` could be redirected from a public page to a private address, and it sent your gateway headers to any site; every web path now goes through one guard that re-checks each redirect and sends only what the site should see, with a provenance line on every fetched page and an honest `User-Agent`. No single key stops running work any more: `Esc`, `Ctrl+L`, `Ctrl+C` and `Ctrl+D` ask first, a stopped reply is kept, and editing an earlier message keeps the turns it replaces. Permission rules now read a command the way its own shell reads it, instruction files are checked for hidden characters and secrets as they load, and terminal agent hooks follow Claude Code's matcher rules, with `~/.claude` hooks opt-in. The terminal agent can add MCP servers from a pasted README snippet (`continuous mcp add`), shows how far a local server has read the prompt, and sessions can be pruned to the trash.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent.

### New

- `cacheBehavior.subagentTtl` sets the prompt cache lifetime of subagent runs on a model: `5m` (the default), `1h`, `auto` (the Auto rules applied to the run's own requests) or `inherit` (what the chat uses). It applies to the subagent tool, Loop workers and `cn` subagents, and is in the model editor. See "Subagents" in the prompt caching docs.
- `CONTINUOUS_FORCE_CACHE_5M=1` is a debug override that puts every prompt cache entry on the 5-minute lifetime, in the editor and in `cn`, over every other lifetime setting.
- A terminal command's approval card says which interpreter the command hands its text to, when that is not the terminal's own shell: **Runs through:** `bash -c`, `bash -lc in WSL`, `bash -c, then pwsh -c`, the login shell on a host reached by `ssh`, or a script, with a note when what runs is not all written in the command. An ordinary command, and one that already says it (`npm test`, `make`, `bash deploy.sh`), gets no line.
- **`cn` shows how far a local server has read the prompt.** On llama.cpp and Strata, the spinner row says "Reading the prompt: 360k of 384k tokens, 16k from the cache, about 18 s left" while a long prompt is read, the same line as the extension's, updated at most once a second, and goes away when the reply starts. Before, a long read showed only the spinner. In `cn -p` the line goes to stderr, at most once every 10 s, and only with `--verbose`. `cn` asks for it only from a local server whose `/props` answers as llama.cpp's does; cloud APIs and other servers are never sent the field.
- Instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, `AGENT.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and rule files) are checked as they load, in the IDE and in `cn`: hidden characters (zero-width, text-direction, tag and other invisible characters) are removed, with a notice naming the file and lines but not the removed text; a value that looks like a key or token gives a warning naming the file and line, and the file still loads as written. In the IDE the notices show above the chat input with a link to the file; `cn` prints each once.
- **Add MCP servers from the terminal.** `continuous mcp add <paste-or-file>` reads what a server's README tells you to paste (Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, Zed, OpenCode, Codex and Devin JSON or TOML, `npx`, `uvx` and `docker run` lines, an `https://` URL, `claude mcp add` and `code --add-mcp` lines, VS Code and Cursor install links) and adds the server to your own `config.yaml`, comments kept. Nothing runs on paste.
  - It shows the exact command or URL and blocks a download run by a shell, `docker --privileged`, a mount of `/` or the Docker socket, and plain `http://` to another host. It warns about unpinned `npx`/`uvx` packages, shell wrappers, risky docker flags and keys written into the snippet.
  - It asks once before a test connection (the test runs the command), lists the server's tools, resources and prompts without calling any, marks descriptions that read like instructions, and gives a fix for a missing Node.js, uv or Docker, a timeout or a sign-in. `--dry-run` connects to nothing and writes nothing.
  - Keys go to `~/.continuous/.env` as `${{ secrets.NAME }}`; a name already in use is refused. See "Add a server from a README snippet" in the MCP docs.
  - `continuous mcp add-json <name> '<json>'` takes one server object. `continuous mcp list` shows the servers in your `config.yaml` and the project's `.continuous/mcpServers/` with secret names, never values. `continuous mcp test <name>` asks, then tests a saved server and exits `1` when it fails. `continuous mcp remove <name>` removes one and keeps its secrets. `--scope project` saves to `.continuous/mcpServers/<name>.yaml` for the project, which starts only after each person trusts the folder. The settings dialog for the same steps is a follow-up.
- `continuous sessions prune --older-than <age>` moves every session last used before the age to the trash, where it can be restored for 7 days with `continuous sessions restore <id>`. It lists them first and asks, or takes `--yes`; `--dry-run` and `--json` report. Sessions open in a window or a running agent are left alone. Nothing deletes sessions by itself: there is no retention period.
- `continuous -p --no-session-persistence` runs without writing the session to disk, so it cannot be resumed.
- `/export` and `continuous export` say how many values were masked, and `--raw` writes the text unmasked, with a warning.
- **Esc stops a reply, after asking.** `Esc` in an empty chat input while a reply streams asks "Stop the response?": `Enter` stops, `Esc` keeps going. What the reply wrote and your unsent text are kept, and the stopped turn is saved for Resume. The Stop button declares the key with `aria-keyshortcuts`. See "Stop, Resume and recovering a turn".
- **Editing an earlier message keeps the replaced turns.** Before the edit runs, the conversation is saved as "<title> (before edit)" in History, and a line above the input offers Undo (the conversation comes back; the edited version is kept in the copy instead) and View. The terminal agent saves the same copy before it rewinds for an edit; `/resume` opens it.
- **The server's own timings are kept with each reply's usage.** From llama.cpp and Strata: how many prompt tokens were read and how many came from the cache, how long the read and the writing took, the write speed, and the speculative draft tokens offered and accepted. From Ollama: the token counts and its durations, including the time to load the model. Nothing is shown yet; the speed display builds on this.
- **Each chat request records what it did and how fast.** From the stream it is already reading, with no extra request: when it was sent, the first event, the first token, the first text or tool call, the phases it went through (waiting, reading the prompt, thinking, writing, writing a tool call), the time to first token, the output speed and the prompt read speed where the server reports one, each marked as the server's figure, measured here, or an estimate from characters. The record is kept with the reply's usage and in the LLM log; the live speed line and the per-reply summary build on it.
- Every fetched page (the fetch tool, `Fetch` in `cn`, and `@url`) starts with one provenance line: final URL, status, size, time, SHA-256 prefix, `robots.txt` verdict (not checked yet) and the rule that allowed it. Every web request, refused ones included, goes to an in-memory fetch log for the session and to the audit trail as a `fetch` line with query values masked.

### Behaviour changes

- Subagent runs now use the 5-minute prompt cache lifetime by default, also when the chat is set to 1 hour: their requests come seconds apart, so a 1-hour entry cost more to write and was rarely read later. Set `cacheBehavior.subagentTtl: inherit` on the model for the old behaviour.
- The request that lists Anthropic models is now sent with `anthropic-version: 2026-10-21`, and again with `2023-06-01` if a gateway answers 400. Messages requests stay on `2023-06-01`.
- **Allow rules read a terminal command the way its shell does.** An allow rule no longer covers text that its shell reads as more commands than the rule sees: a lone carriage return, bash's `$'...'`, or a comment followed by another line, in every shell. In PowerShell and cmd the shell's own reading must also be understood, and each command it finds must be covered by an allow rule. In PowerShell this means an allow rule no longer covers a command holding `$`, `(`, `{`, `#`, `!`, `@`, a backtick, `&&` or `||`, or a redirect other than to `$null`: such a command follows your level instead (headless, one that would ask is refused). `cn`'s `Bash(...)` allows get the same check. Deny and ask rules are unchanged.
- PowerShell's curly quotes, en and em dashes and Unicode spaces: a PowerShell command holding one is no longer vouched read-only, and deny rules, ask rules and protected paths also meet its ASCII spelling (`git “push”` is `git push` there). `Get-Process -ComputerName` is no longer vouched as a local read, because it asks another machine.
- **In a remote window (SSH, a WSL window, a dev container, Codespaces) a terminal command is judged as read by an unknown shell, not by this machine's.** Such a command is never vouched read-only and never covered by an allow rule, so it follows your level; deny and ask rules read it under every grammar. Before, it was judged by the editor machine's shell (PowerShell on a Windows laptop for a command a remote bash reads). The command lint's dialect checks and the missing-program check no longer run for a remote window, so `cd app && npm test` is no longer refused on a Windows laptop before it reaches a remote bash.
- With `$SHELL` set to a shell the permission engine does not parse (fish, nushell, ksh), allow rules no longer cover terminal commands, in the IDE and in `cn` (`Bash(...)` rules): the call follows your level, and headless one that would ask is refused.
- Deny and ask rules read a PowerShell `-EncodedCommand` decoded, under every spelling PowerShell takes (`-e`, `-ec`, `-enc`, `/e`, any case, nested). One that cannot be decoded matches every deny and ask rule, and every floor rule. The audit record of a terminal command now names the shell it was read with and whether that is known (`reading.shell`, `reading.shellSource`).
- Terminal agent hooks: hooks in Claude Code's user settings (`~/.claude/settings.json`) no longer run unless you opt in with `"hooks": { "readClaudeSettings": true }` in `~/.continuous/settings.json`. If that file has hooks and the setting is not there, the first start prints a one-time notice naming the file and the setting; `continuous hooks` lists them as skipped. Project `.claude/` files are unchanged and still run once you trust the project.
- Terminal agent hooks: a hook `matcher` is read the way Claude Code reads it. A matcher of only letters, digits, `_`, `-`, spaces, `,` and `|` is an exact tool name or a list of names, so `Edit` no longer matches `MultiEdit` or `NotebookEdit` and `Edit|Write` matches exactly those two; any other character still makes an unanchored regular expression (`mcp__.*`, `Notebook.*`, `^Edit$`). A matcher that relied on matching part of a name needs a `.*`.
- Terminal agent hooks: a `Stop` hook that blocks (exit 2, or `decision: "block"`) now sends the agent back to work with its reason as the next message, instead of being logged and ignored. At most three continuations follow each of your messages; a fourth block ends the turn with a notice. Claude Code allows eight.
- In a workspace VS Code has not trusted (Restricted Mode), `AGENTS.md` (or `AGENT.md`, `CLAUDE.md`) is no longer read. A line above the chat input offers **Load**, which reads it for that window only and saves nothing; trusting the workspace reads it from then on. `cn` is unchanged here.
- An instruction file longer than 32 KiB is cut after the last whole line that fits, with a line naming the file where it was cut and a notice saying how many lines were loaded. Before, the whole file was sent.
- A session at IDGAF now says so once: "IDGAF is on for this session only: your rules, locked rules and protected files stop nothing; each call runs and the audit trail records what would have stopped it. Tools you switched off stay off." In the extension it is a dismissible line above the input, once per chat session; in `cn` one line in the chat or on stderr, naming `--auto` or `--policy` when a flag turned it on. It is a notice, never a question. The audit trail records it as an `idgaf-session` setting change, and a loosening that comes from the environment (`CONTINUOUS_HEADLESS_LEGACY_ALLOW=1`) as a separate `env-loosening` record; that variable's start-up line now says it holds for every headless run while it is set.
- `cn --resume` of a session that ran at IDGAF starts at your configured levels, as before, and now says so in one line: "Resumed at your configured levels: this session ran at IDGAF, and IDGAF is not restored." Pass `--policy idgaf` to turn it on again. Session files written by `cn` record which areas were at IDGAF (`idgafAreas`). In the extension, IDGAF still survives a reload of the chat panel or the extension host within the same editor session.
- In `cn` Plan mode at Questions IDGAF, "Build this plan?" is no longer asked: the turn ends with the plan file saved and Plan mode kept, as the extension's plan card already does. Below IDGAF the question is unchanged.
- Plan edits at Automatic now works as Permissive until a reviewer for plans exists, and its description says so ("In Loop, as Permissive until a plan reviewer exists"). A re-plan that adds more new to-dos than the Plan edits cap (default 5) now waits for you; before, Automatic let any re-plan go on with no cap.
- "Always on" / "Always-on" rules are now called **locked rules** everywhere (the Permissions page badge and Locks card, the Custom policy list, the first-run tip, rule refusals and the docs), so they are not confused with the **Always** list. The `floor:` key in `permissions.yaml` is unchanged. The IDGAF descriptions now say that locked rules are ignored too, which is what IDGAF has done since 2.16.2.
- `/export --json` (the session file `/import` reads) now replaces secrets the at-rest scanner recognises with `[REDACTED:<kind>:xxxx]` and says how many; before, it wrote the session as it was. `/export --json --raw` keeps the old behaviour.
- `continuous clean --yes` moves old sessions to the trash instead of deleting them, so a clean can be undone with `continuous sessions restore <id>` for 7 days, and it leaves sessions open in another window or a running agent alone. Logs and `dev_data` are deleted as before.
- Feedback (thumbs up or down on a reply) sends the full prompt of the newest request only. Every other request sends its size and SHA-256 in place of the prompt; before, it sent `[prompt not kept: older request]` and nothing else.
- **No single key stops running work.** `Ctrl+L`, New Session, opening a chat from History and switching, closing or archiving a session tab now ask "Stop the agent and start a new chat?" (or open, or switch) while a reply streams, a tool call waits for approval, a tool runs or a loop runs. `Enter` stops the work the way Stop does and switches, saving the chat with its reply marked stopped; `Esc` keeps working. Pressing the key again or holding it never answers. With nothing running nothing is asked, so there is no "don't ask again". The Command Palette's **Stop Response**, and the Stop button reached with `Enter` or `Space`, ask the same way; a click on Stop still stops at once.
- **Terminal agent: `Esc`, `Ctrl+C` and `Ctrl+D` ask first.** `Esc` while the agent works, and `Ctrl+C` on an empty prompt while it works, ask "Stop the response? enter to stop · esc to keep going". `Ctrl+C` with text typed no longer clears it at once: it asks "Clear the input?", and `Up` brings cleared text back. Two `Ctrl+C` presses within a second exit at once only while idle; while a turn, a tool call or a loop runs they ask "Exit and stop the agent?", and a held key's auto-repeat never counts as the second press. `Ctrl+D` asks the same while work runs or text is typed.
- **Terminal agent: a stopped reply is kept.** What the model wrote before Stop stays in the conversation and is saved with the session, marked as stopped; `Enter` on the empty prompt resumes from it instead of asking again from scratch.
- **Terminal agent: `Esc` on a permission prompt skips that call.** `Esc` (or `Ctrl+C`) is now "No, skip this call": the model gets the denied result and the turn goes on. "No, and tell Continue what to do differently" (`n`) still ends the turn, after asking "Stop the response?".
- **Sites now see who is fetching.** The fetch tool, `Fetch` in `cn`, `@url` and the favicon lookup send `User-Agent: Continuous-User/<major>.<minor> (+https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/web-agent.md)` instead of `node-fetch`; the docs crawler sends `Continuous-Crawler/<major>.<minor> (+…)` instead of `node-fetch` (Cheerio) or a Chrome 88 string (Chromium); `@web`, `search_web` and `@google` send `Continuous-User/<major>.<minor>` alone. The string carries no operating system, editor, patch version or id. Pages read for you ask for Markdown first (`Accept: text/markdown, text/html;q=0.9, …`). A site that blocked `node-fetch` may now let the request through, and one that blocks unknown agents may refuse it: `web.userAgent` in your own config.yaml chooses `generic-agent`, a browser preset or a custom string, and `web.hosts.<pattern>.userAgent` does it for some hosts only. `robots.txt` is checked as `Continuous-User` whatever you choose. A project or assistant config cannot change any of this.
- `web.acceptLanguage`, `web.hosts.<pattern>.headers` and `web.limits.maxRedirects` are now in force. A per-host header goes only to hosts that match the pattern and not to a redirect elsewhere; `maxRedirects` (default 5, ceiling 10) applies to every path on the guarded fetch, and a project or assistant config may only lower it.

### Fixes

- Protected paths recognise Windows 8.3 short names with punctuation or a number past 9 (`GIT-CR~1` for `.git-credentials`, `VAULT-~1`, `GIT-C~10`).
- An "Auto-answered: question -> answer" line stays one line when the answer holds a line break.
- **Ollama's native API now reports usage.** A reply from an `ollama` model had no token counts at all; it now has the prompt and reply counts, the cached part of the prompt, and Ollama's timings.
- **The "a re-read would take about N s" estimate on Ollama after a cache hit.** Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint counts cached tokens in its prompt read speed, so after a cache hit the speed was too high and the estimate too short. The speed is now worked out from the tokens Ollama actually read.
- **The LLM console's "To First Token" on llama.cpp and Strata.** It counted from the first prompt-progress update, a second or two in, instead of the first token, and "Tokens/s" included most of the prompt read. Both now come from the request's timing record.
- **Security: `@url` followed redirects to private addresses and sent your gateway headers to any site.** A public page named with `@url` could redirect to the cloud metadata service (`169.254.169.254`) or another private or loopback address, and Continuous followed it (up to 20 hops) and gave the reply to the model. `@url` also sent every `requestOptions.headers` value, often a gateway or proxy token, to whatever site you named, and `@web`, the `search_web` tool and `@google` sent them to the search service. Now `@url`, the favicon lookup and the search paths go through the same guard as the fetch tool: at most five redirects, every hop checked again, a redirect to a non-public or link-local address refused, the connection pinned to the address that was checked (no DNS rebinding), and the global headers sent only to your model endpoints. Upgrade if you use `@url` on a machine that can reach a metadata service or an internal network, or if your `requestOptions.headers` carry a credential.
- The fetch guard now treats every IANA special-purpose block that is not globally reachable as private (documentation, benchmarking, `192.0.0.0/24`, `2001:db8::/32`, `100::/64` and others, from the registry itself), refuses a redirect whose address carries a credential, and drops `Authorization` and `Cookie` when a redirect changes origin.
- Favicons must be raster images of at most 256 KiB, fetched within 5 seconds; an SVG icon is no longer embedded. The search response is capped at the fetch size limit with a deadline, and search and fetch errors give the HTTP status without quoting the response body.

### Upgrade notes

- **Hooks from Claude Code.** Hooks in `~/.claude/settings.json` no longer run in the terminal agent until you add `"hooks": { "readClaudeSettings": true }` to your Continuous `settings.json`.
- **Restricted Mode.** In a workspace VS Code has not trusted, `AGENTS.md` is not read until you choose Load above the chat input.
- **Scripts.** `continuous clean --json` lists sessions under `sessions` and exits 1 when a move or deletion fails.
- **Sites you fetch** now see `Continuous-User/<major>.<minor>` instead of `node-fetch`; set `web.userAgent` in your own config to change it.
- **Firewalls and sandboxes.** No new host.
